title: Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds
main_claim: Theorem 1.2: Let (X,Δ) be a klt pair on a globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold with rational boundary. Then it has a finite program of ordinary negative steps starting on X. The program ends at a nef adjoint when K_X+Δ is pseudo-effective and at a Mori fibre space otherwise. Global Weil Q-factoriality, klt, the canonical datum and (optionally) strong Q-factoriality are preserved along the way.

issues.description: Lemma 3.1 (integral descent) needs f to be a projective bimeromorphic contraction. Here it is applied to the contraction f of a Q_{i,T}-negative ray taken from the generalized HX2026 Thm 1.5 program, whose adjoint has a transcendental nef part λ_i H. The proof never states why this generalized flipping contraction is projective. Prop 6.1 does justify projectivity for its own contractions, by citing HX2026 Prop 4.2 and Lemmas 2.39-2.40. The same citations probably cover this case, so this is a missing justification, not an error.
issues.evidence: "For the ordinary rational klt pair (T,B^j_T), the line bundle M_j=ℓ_jP^j_T is numerically trivial over Z ... Lemma~\ref{lem:descent} gives an actual line bundle M_{j,Z} with M_j=f^*M_{j,Z}."

issues.description: Finiteness of the marked models φ_i rests on the finiteness theorem for weak log canonical models (HX2026 Thm 5.15). The targets X_i are only globally Weil Q-factorial, not strongly Q-factorial. The paper simply asserts that the cited theorem needs neither rationality nor strong Q-factoriality. I could not check this against HX2026.
issues.evidence: "This real segment is allowed in the finiteness theorem for weak log canonical models \cite[Theorem~5.15]{HX2026}; neither rationality of H nor strong Q-factoriality of X is required there."

coverage:
I read every section in full: 01 introduction, 02 analytic, 03 steps, 04 terminal, 05 scaling, 06 perturbation, 07 endpoints, and the start of appendix 13. I checked these in detail:
- Negativity and strict comparison: Lemma 2.4 (iii)-(v).
- The trace relation and bigness of H_T: Lemma 2.5 and Cor 2.6.
- Integral descent: Lemma 3.1.
- The support class with a Kähler margin: Lemma 3.2.
- Ordinary steps and transport of classes: Prop 3.4 and Lemma 3.5, including the sign of J_{T'}.
- Cycle loss: Lemma 4.1.
- The low-place counts, including the k-th blowup coefficient -k(1-b): Lemmas 4.3 and 4.6.
- Real-boundary terminal fourfold termination (Prop 4.7): the flipped-surface witness set, the c_2 count for flipping surfaces inside the boundary, and the final c_2 drop.
- The scaling construction and the convexity argument for the negative ray: Prop 5.1.
- λ_i→0: Lemma 5.2.
- Stabilizing the extraction set and terminality of the limit: Prop 5.3.
- Exclusion of divisorial and fibre steps: Prop 6.1.
- The rational nef polytope (Shokurov/Birkar length bound -8): Lemma 6.2.
- The gap (m-1)c>8 and the amplified adjoint mQ-(m-1)P: Prop 6.4 (1)-(4).
- The final descent to Z_i that forces D_i·R_i=0: Prop 6.5.
- The endpoint lemmas 7.1 and 7.2.
- The appendix's node example (K_U=H|_U+E): verified.
Cited results from HX2026, Fujino2022 and DHP2024 were taken on trust and not checked.
